utterances.text: It now functions again, as far as I am informed. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will proceed then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I think that, a minute ago, you said that you didn't know the exact locations of the totality of these brigades. I am going to ask you the question, Witness, before we stop for a break a little earlier today. My question is: Did you know where the control and command posts at the level of battalions were located for each of these brigades?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To ask me to recall these locations at this time without my own personal map is -- it shows lack of knowledge of the tactical situation on the ground. I knew my way --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will interrupt you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...the answers that you don't know them. There is nothing wrong with not knowing them. Mr. Thomas, the Defence may ask the questions it would like to ask you. Whether you find them wise or intelligent or silly or stupid is not of any importance. The Defence asks the questions and if you would please answer them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I just make one comment, that he said that I did not know where they were. I said I knew where they were at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, please. Unfortunately, I am not questioning you with regard to in the past, but I am questioning you today. Witness, am I to assume that your answer would be the same for the command and control posts of companies?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have a better chance of showing you on the ground. The answer is, at this time, I can't show you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: It would be a pleasure to go the Sarajevo with you but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...would you please refrain from commenting on the answers. If you want --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that this would be an ideal moment to stop. Mr. President, I think that you told us that we could go as far as we could, and I don't think that we can go much further, we can proceed much further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...to the witness and you may indicate, not out of irritation, but when the subject matter you would like to deal with is completed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you answer by saying "yes" or "no"? My first question: Are you capable of answering a question by saying "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That is what I was afraid of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's stop having a debate between witness and counsel. I both call upon you, Mr. Thomas, and on you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, otherwise, I will have to intervene and have -- at any specific question, have to decide on whether it can be answered by "yes" or "no." Mr. Thomas, do your utmost best to see whether you can answer the questions by "yes" or "no." Yes? Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, may I assume that your answer would be the same to a question regarding the command and control posts of companies?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Witness, could you please have a look at this page which finishes with the number 57.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could you ask the witness to approach the microphone, for the sake of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please assist -- I am sorry, I have forgotten to put on my microphone. Would you please speak as good as you can into the microphone, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you have this document in front of you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. At the bottom of this page, the one -- the paragraph which is just before the last one, can you see a list of weapons? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the abbreviation, the acronym, "MA" or "ML" 150 corresponds to?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 150 millimetre is the calibre of gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, my question was: What do the acronyms "ML" -- what does the acronym "ML" stand for?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, as you can see in the transcript, it was presumably translated - although I am following the direct channel - the acronym "MA" or "ML." But you are asking about "ML." Mr. Thomas, could you please tell us what "ML" stands for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In fact, as I understand it, it is "M-1."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. What stand then "M-1" for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a calibre of gun -- that is a calibre of -- it is a type of gun, and it is probably found in the Yugoslav army handbook, the exact type of gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Q Very well. But do you know what the corresponds to, what this acronym stands for?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It stands for a type of gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: We have understood that. Do you know what it corresponds to, yes or no? And if "yes" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What type of gun is M-1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is an artillery piece.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A specific one or --?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a specific one, and I would look it up in my handbook to identify it correctly, exactly what -- but it is an artillery Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. piece that fires a 150-millimetre shell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I understand your answer is that you could not indicate what weapon it stands for but it does stand for a type of weapon which you would have to look up to know for sure what specific type?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To be precise, yes, I would look it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it correct, Witness, that "MOR" that we can see below stands for a mortar? This abbreviation stands for a mortar?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it true that the figures 3-4 that we can see by the side mean that there were three or 4 mortars of 120 millimetres which were identified?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that they reported that these weapons were known to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like you to provide me with a similar type of answer for what we can see in front of mortars of 82 millimetres, 82-millimetre calibre mortars. Were there between two and five mortar pieces which were identified by the services in question?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first, this UNPROFOR report was not necessarily military observer, but it tells you that between two to five mortars were suspected in that location, because the exact number couldn't be determined.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So the answer is "yes." Witness, what does "BP" stand for? What does the abbreviation "BP" stand for?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: BP is put in front of numbers that is used on a specific map sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Since this is specific and you knew about it, could you tell us what it refers to?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map is divided into coordinates and each of these coordinates, because the numbers repeat themselves, the coordinates are given letters to assist in identification. Is this clear enough or do you want further explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No. Perhaps we will require other clarifications from you at a later stage. Thank you. Witness, I would like you to read in the upper part of the paragraph that you have in front of you - if you can find your glasses or if you need them - approximately how many men were there in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I read this paragraph, it says: "Estimated approximately 25.000 men." Both of these are terms in English we use to be -- about a situation which there is no definitive answer. Estimated and approximated 25.000 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That is perfect. Was that the so-called BH army?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This army was identified by us as the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I am going to try to ask you questions with regard to the Bosnian army on the one hand, the so-called government army, and how did you call -- what did you call the other army, if you please, the Serbian army?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bosnian army was called the Bosnian army and the Serb army was called the Bosnian Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So I will try to refer to them as such. Witness, is it true that you made a written statement before giving testimony and you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is it true, Witness, that as part of this statement, with regard to the strategy of the Bosnian army, you stated that: "People from the Bosnian army wanted to use the town on a strategic level as a reservoir to enable soldiers to come in or go out with regard to other fronts and, in particular, with regard to Gorazde or other pockets."

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either the English hasn't come across clearly or he has misstated my testimony that I gave in 1998. I would like to see a copy of the witness statement or to have it rephrased.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I shall show you your statement in a minute. But is this something that you said, roughly speaking?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't capture what I said at all to the person from this Tribunal that interviewed me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. We will see about that in a minute. Witness, did you state that a certain amount of shelling -- that civilian zones were shelled to a certain extent and in a purely random manner?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can't confirm that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question at this moment was: Is that what you stated? If you say, "I stated in a certain context" - I am not asking you now to add any context - but if it was in a certain context and you would like to explain briefly, you are allowed to do so. But you are not allowed to add the context now, because you were asked about your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to have a copy of the witness statement that I gave in 1998. I have, of course, one in the witness room, but I can't recall exactly in this room exactly what the wording I used when I talked to the Tribunal in 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, when you are referring to the statement of the witness, he expressed quite clearly that he would like to be confronted with this --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He will be confronted in a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...to the last question. He would already like to be confronted with at least the words in the statement. So would you please read that slowly to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But I will reformulate my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, in the examination-in-chief, you answered a few questions about the shelling of civilian areas. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have answered questions about the questions of civilian areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: As regards to those civilian areas, Witness, the question is the following: As a tank officer, how can you formally and definitely exclude the presence of mobile military targets of any sort which would be located in a civilian zone, what one can consider to be a civilian zone, when firing is ongoing?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is difficult to answer in just "yes" or "no." It depends whether I am already on the ground or whether I am arriving after to determine my conclusions. Do you want me to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No. I will reframe my question. Witness, you observed -- were observing firing in a zone that you considered to be a civilian area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How, if you can -- how can you categorically rule out that, at the moment of the firing, or perhaps a bit before the firing, there hadn't been on that particular spot a kind of military mobile object?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some cases, I couldn't rule out; in some cases, I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I shall note down your answer because you said that, in some cases, it could not be excluded. Could you tell me, please, why could this not be excluded?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because in one case that comes to mind, I could see one of my OPs being shelled, and the military observers in that location definitely confirmed that there was no other military people in that presence, in that area, except themselves and the civilians that lived in their accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are referring to very specific situation where the command posts themselves were affected. I am not saying targeted, but touched, hit.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you rephrase your question, because I am not sure what you are trying to question me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In the cases that you have been talking about, that is, situations in which the observation posts are -- these situations directly relate to command -- to observation posts?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situations reflect my observation post, and there is no military post adjacent to it because our practice was to keep military posts from either belligerent away from our OP location, except if we had a liaison function there. I can specifically detail cases of where we observed artillery fire on the ground, hitting civilians, and we knew that there were nobody else in that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Please try, since you understand French perfectly, to follow my question. The cases that you mentioned are cases where the UN observation posts were -- that had to do with the UN observation posts directly? I shall not continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was: Whether the cases you mentioned are case where the UN observations posts were -- that had to do with the UN observations post directly. You nodded, but unfortunately, in the transcript, nodding doesn't appear. It cannot be translated. So would you please answer in words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The cases I referred to are ones that I can categorically say there were no UN -- there were no military presence there because I had military observers there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you were referring to UN observation posts. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So your reply -- would you like a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, put your next question to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, your reply was that those cases relate to situations where the military observers were directly targeted?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Directly concerned is the word. I have to follow both. Were directly involved.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That isn't correct. These are cases that I can categorically say that military observers saw civilians being shelled, but there was no Bosnian presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So you are telling us that what the military observers say are correct, as a rule, are correct and can be verified?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would like to give you some documents, I just want to number them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we will be referring to number 114, then we shall have number 115. [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any translation problem because -- [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Receiving the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are the two languages separated again? Yes, then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I answered directly. It is all right now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the interpreters have not received these papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there is practically nothing to translate and that is the reason why.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you have the document 114 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, is it a document that comes from the services that you were responsible for at a given period of time?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It appears to be a document issued by the French sector headquarters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to raise an objection on two grounds. The first one is the documents appear, on their face of it, to be outside the time period that the witness was in Sarajevo; and second of all, as is obvious from the face of the documents, these are Rule 70 documents, and if my learned colleague intends on going into the contents of these documents, I would respectfully request that we do so in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's first deal with the first one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, your first objection is denied since, even if it would be outside of the period -- if it would be outside the period in which the witness was functioning in Sarajevo, it could be relevant in a general assessment of the position, since the witness also had to rely on those supporting him and then the period of time is not always decisive. As far as the second issue is concerned, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you just do some arithmetics, it might not affect the confidant of the documents, but if you refer to dates, times and if it comes to anything more, we should turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is only a question of arithmetics and logic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And whatever reference to times and type of, and just refer to lines so that we can all follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I would like to mention that I have not received a full answer from you about the question of translation, but I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you have in front of you that document. Could you read item 2. I think this is possible, this sentence that is in front.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to para 2 or item 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I said item 2.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can just read it so I can make sure I am reading the paragraph, you are reading: "The following outgoing fire was observed from Presidency positions, artillery, nil; mortars, nil."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Would you now read what you have just read under item 3.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "The following incoming fire was observed on Serb controlled areas." Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: A and B?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Artillery 13, mortar 46."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you read C, "MRL"?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is that an abbreviation for a multiple rocket launcher?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you have AAA -- an AAA gun, an anti-aircraft gun, an AAA?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You don't see any AAAs in that document?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a heading for AAA, but there is no quantity shown next to that item.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: My question did not relate to the number of shots. It was a question about the abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "AAA" stands for anti-aircraft.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How can you, if you can, explain the mathematical coherence -- incoherence?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between what items?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, don't you see any mathematical incoherence in that document?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The problem is that this document was almost six to eight months before I arrived in Sarajevo --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer this question because it was too far in advance of my time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if there is any mathematical incoherence, would you please tell the witness in what respect so he can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, according to your military observers, it is exact that 13 artillery impacts were received on the Serb side; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this report, that is what is stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And according to the report and the military observers, there were no artillery -- there was no artillery fire from the side of the Presidency; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I ask you to quote this document correctly?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It says that: "No outgoing artillery fire was observed from Presidency positions." That is what it says. Your question said: "That according to your military observers is it exact that 13 artillery impacts were received" -- first you mentioned -- you mix up observations and numbers. So would you please be very precise in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that from the Presidency positions, on that day, no artillery firing was observed on that day, according to this document?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would also call the attention of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please first answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That means that the military observers did not observe any fire, but there is a caveat written at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: We will go back to this in a while, if it is necessary. Is it correct, Witness, that from the Presidency position side there were no mortar, there was no mortar firing observed under item 2?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no mortar fire observed by military observers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the sake of the translation, because it comes down to the very precise meaning of the words, in page 63, line 9, the English transcript says: "There was no mortar firing observed." And I heard that Mr. Piletta-Zanin said "noter" in French which means, as far as I am correct, doesn't mean "not observed," but "not put on paper." Not noted down; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would say that I don't remember the term used. It is more or less the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, now I would like to provide you with a second group of documents, numbers 115 -- I apologise. You already have 115. Now, the next number is 116. So 115 has already been distributed. Witness, can we do the same sort of exercise. What sort of document is this?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a daily sit-rep issued by one of my predecessors several months before I ever was in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you please read the same items.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The following outgoing fire was observed from the Serb positions and only 12 outgoing artillery rounds are noted as being observed. The other categories are nil. The following outgoing fire was observed from Presidency positions," which I assume to be Bosnian because we didn't use this term. "Artillery," the only one is 12 -- the only category is 12 mortar rounds were observed by military observers. In "incoming," that is what "inc-rep" stands for to clarify for those who are not aware yet, "The following incoming fire was observed on Serb controlled areas and we have 26 mortar rounds as reported impacting on Serb controlled areas." Then we talk about, "The following incoming fire was observed." And I would ask the interpreters to take note of the term and point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas, if the interpreters need any specific guidance, I will give it to them and if you think they should be given, you should address me, not to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it is almost time to make a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But I would like the witness to simply read the last figure that he was about to read a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The following incoming fire was observed on Bosnian-controlled areas: Artillery, 4; mortar, 32; tank, nil; MRS, nil; AAA, nil."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, do you know how many multiple launchers did the Sarajevo forces, that is the forces of the Presidency, have?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many?

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You can look it up in the document given to the Court in the weapons collections point documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The Chamber has received nothing. If you know how many, tell us; if you don't --

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS ROY THOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you be able to tell if you could consult --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it is a time to make a break and at this stage. The Defence would like the break that it had requested before. I think it would be excellent time for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would mean that we continue at 6.00, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That means that we would like to stop here. The Defence would like to have a break now and that we should stop now as I had asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is how far the Defence comes today. Then we have another issue to discuss and that is, Mr. Thomas, would you, although I know that your travel schedule was foreseen to return this evening, but as you might have noticed, the examination and cross-examination is not concluded yet. Would you be available next Monday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your flexibility in your programme. We will then adjourn until next Monday at 9.00 in the morning, same courtroom. Mr. Mundis, is there still -- oh, you have the letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I do, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have to keep the map for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that would be easier. That would be easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Travelling with these maps is not that simple for us. Is there anything else, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If, perhaps, I believe I need to offer a brief explanation with respect to the letter, if that is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As explanation in respect of the letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I have, Mr. President, copies of the letter from the French government. There have been certain redactions made to the French letter because it relates to the travel arrangements and security arrangements with respect to one of the witnesses. I am prepared to allow the Bench to see the original to confirm what has been redacted, however, I have been requested to obtain the original copy and only distribute the redacted versions, if I may be allowed to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we could see at this very moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely, and I do have a copy for the Defence and a copy for the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Usher, you could, since this does not affect in any way Mr. Thomas, perhaps you could escort him out of the courtroom. We will see you back at 9.00 in the morning next Monday, Mr. Thomas. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the Chamber has checked whether the redacted part of the letter would contain anything of any importance for the Defence. It just contains the arrangements of a meeting with the OTP, times, places, et cetera, which are requested to be kept secret. Nothing else. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Agreed. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, please return this to Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Anything else at this very moment? If not, we will, although it is a bit difficult, adjourn for the second -- Judge Nieto-Navia has something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I would like to point out that the letter of the Minister of Foreign Affairs, says or mentions "aide-memoire," a memory aid. I think that the Prosecutor should have mentioned that in the memorandum just to help us to understand what kind of papers we are dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Our apologies for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there is nothing else, I now, almost for the third time, adjourn until next Monday morning, same courtroom. I wish you a good weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
